groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: We are down to two candidates for one position, and we need to decide by the end of the day in order to finalize this whole procedure.
M: Yes, but it isn't an easy choice to make. Both applicants are quite strong.
W: Let's get to it, then. Both of them went to good universities, and both of them studied business-related subjects. So academically, I'd say they're pretty much the same. What do you think?
M: I would agree, yes. The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university. But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter.
W: That's true, and worth noting. Thank you. In addition, Rachel interviewed very well. I thought she came across as bright and alert.
M: Yes. She asked some very good questions about the position and the company, which made me think she is very keen about the job.
W: I thought so, too. Now, let's look at Peter's interview performance. I thought he also did very well. He came across as respectful and professional, wouldn't you say? Calm and poised. Very mature for his age.
M: Exactly. In my notes, I wrote that he seemed composed and in control of his emotions. I think he definitely looked more mature than Rachel.
W: Interesting. So, we agree that Rachel appeared inexperienced and less mature than Peter, even though both candidates are the same age and have practically no work experience.
M: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow. Maybe it was something about their body language.
W: Sure. Maybe he was simply less nervous.
M: Maybe. Who knows? To be honest, I think I like Rachel better.
W: Hmm. Really? I think I like Peter.
M: Ah, well. If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: We're here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L'Orange, to discuss her latest collection. Ms. Ortega, how would you describe this season's look?
W: To be honest, my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side, and I think this collection is even more so. I try not to adhere to social norms and expectations. Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic.
M: The assortments of accessories in this collection have had quite the impact on critics. The dazzling cape deployed at the end of the show, for example, bewildered many in the audience. What was your inspiration for this piece?
W: Over the summer, I traveled through rural mountain villages throughout Asia in search of handicrafts to decorate my new studio with. The embroidery done by the women in a particular village was so exquisite. I couldn't stop thinking about it. Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile. So instead, I applied my own eccentric approach. Using glitter, I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape. This ended up in the glamorous, luminous look that concluded the show.
M: It was indeed majestic, and yet, dare I say, masculine at the same time.
W: Well, yes, that was intentional. I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum. Hence, the sparkling cape was paired with a traditional power suit you would typically see in a business setting. It was sensational, if I do say so myself.
M: Spectacular for sure! A stunning show all around. Going against stereotypes, the incorporation of indigenous aspects, along with your underlying signature touch, made this collection a statement of the season. You have proven yourself a formidable young designer, and we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Pet dogs can often readily understand a wide range of their owners' commands and gestures, but are these abilities inborn or are they exclusively learned through training? To find out, a new study examined whether stray dogs could understand human gestures. The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training. The results suggest that dogs can understand complex gestures by simply watching humans. This could have implications in reducing conflict between stray dogs and humans.
Dogs were domesticated 10,000 to 15,000 years ago. This means they are probably the oldest domesticated animals on the planet. Humans then bred dogs with the most desirable and useful traits so that they could function as companions and workers. This resulted in domesticated dogs that are highly responsive to human commands and gestures. However, it was not clear whether dogs understand us through training alone, or whether this was an inherent ability. Why does this matter?
Stray dogs are a common feature in cities around the world. They may observe and occasionally interact with people, but such dogs have never been trained, and are behaviorally "wild". Conflicts between stray dogs and humans are a problem. Understanding how humans shape stray dogs' behavior may help alleviate this problem. According to the researchers of the new study, stray dogs are intelligent creatures. They closely observe humans and use their understanding of us to make a decision. Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect, and giving them space, the researchers assert, can reduce much conflict.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air? Not so! The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between. Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.
The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria, which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 degrees Celsius. As a result, refrigerators are typically set at or below that low end to protect foods against bacteria. Although it might seem like time spent organizing the fridge will spoil your day, doing so will actually make it more user-friendly, easier to clean and food safety-conscious.
Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don't maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there. The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don't need extra-chilly temperatures. Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf. The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here. Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you ran out of room up top. The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible longer. Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how it affects our immune system. So the current projects that I'm quite excited about are looking at older people and factors that are important to them.
In one project we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event and we're trying to understand the impact of depression. Often people in hospital with a hip fracture develop depression, and these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly than others. They get infections. Often these infections lead to death. So we're trying to slow down that progression to feebleness. So if we can better understand how these factors interact, then we can actually start doing something about it.
The impact that my research will have in Birmingham, first of all, is obviously for older people because these are the people that are having hip fractures and developing depression, and we're trying to improve their health and their quality of life. But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK. This is a problem globally. People are aging. There's a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives. So the last part of their life can often be full of ill health, and we're trying to understand factors that can contribute to the quality of life later on.
I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant. Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them. Whereas I feel that the work I do is relevant to everyone because everyone is aging. Health is an issue for everyone, regardless of their age, and what I'm trying to do is understand the factors that affect health and how we can improve the quality of life in people. So that's one of the things that really excites me about it. One of the other things is, rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Americans are obsessed with celebrity chefs. We talk about them and try to eat like them. But could we learn something more from them than recipes and techniques?
According to market data enterprises, Americans spend nearly 10 billion dollars a year on self-help and personal-organization products. The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do.
Perhaps the principles of cooking organization can be extended to help even those of us who aren't top chefs. The system that makes kitchens function is called "mise-en-place", or literally "put in place". It's a French phrase that means to gather and arrange the ingredients and tools needed for cooking.
But for many professional cooks, the phrase means something deeper. Some cooks call it their religion. It helps them coordinate vast amounts of labor and material, and transforms the lives of its practitioners through focus and self-discipline. Students at the culinary institute of America view it as a way of life. It's a way of concentrating their mind to only focus on the aspects that they need to be working on at the moment, to kind of rid themselves of distractions. And it's a habit that some students carry with them even when they're not in the kitchen. They mise-en-place their life. They set up their books for class. They set up their chef whites. They shine their shoes. They know everything that they need every step of the day.
Then how does one attain this level of organization? The key to high-level organization is the mindset. Cooks can easily do six hours of preparation for a three-hour dinner shift. "Mise-en-place forces cooks to account for every minute of their time and every movement. Every component of one single dish is in one single corner, so their hand literally moves inches," explains Dwayne Lipuma, an instructor at the culinary institute of America. "Once students set up their station, I should be able to cover up their eyes. And they should know that their knives are always here, their oil is always right here, their salt and pepper is always right here."
But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious, your self-respect and the respect of others are precious. Use them wisely. Isn't that a philosophy for our time?

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Why do we stop making goals for ourselves and stop progressing in life? One reason is the belief that we should accept who we are and not constantly strive to improve ourselves. The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth. When we're not growing, learning and seeking improvements in our lives, we tend to stagnate, accepting what is, and stop believing we can be better.
A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination. Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting. Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals, we feel we are always falling short. That leads to disappointment, and we stop dreaming. We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be, quickly finding ourselves shattered by the pain of our reality.
Up until now, unless we work in the creative industry, we've found the idea of using "play" a bit childish. In the West, we're mostly operating from our heads, the rational mind. But it's beginning to be better understood, because using our imagination is actually one of the most powerful things we could ever do.
The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not. What happens, therefore, is that we end up feeling like we're never going to reach our goals. And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction and unhappiness. We measure against the goal, rather than where we've come from. Dan Sullivan calls this "the gap and the gain". We measure always against the goal, which we never feel we're reaching, rather than the gain, that is where we've come from. In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results. We see things we've taken for granted, or not noticed. It's a simple, yet profound change in perception, and what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear. It's so, so simple, yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.

questions.prompt: Why does the man think it is difficult to make the decision?
options: They have to make a choice by the end of the day.
Both candidates are very keen on getting the job.
They hold different views on the procedure.
Both candidates are quite competitive.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the man think it is difficult to make the decision? 

 【翻译】 为什么男士认为很难做出决定? 
 A)  他们必须在今天结束前做出选择。 
 B)  两位候选人都非常渴望得到这份工作。 
 C)  他们对程序持有不同看法。 
 D)  两位候选人都很有竞争力。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Both candidates are quite competitive. 
 【定位】 P2 M: Yes, but it isn't an easy choice to make. Both applicants are quite strong. 
 男：是啊，但这不是个容易做的选择。两位申请者都相当强。 

 【信号】 男士应答里的转折 + 给因 。这是男士对女士「今天得定」的直接应答，but it isn't an easy choice to make 用 but 转出「不好选」，紧接 Both applicants are quite strong 给出原因——两人都很强，正是「难选」的答案句。 

 【替换】 Both applicants are quite strong ↔ Both candidates are quite competitive 近义改写 strong→competitive、applicants→candidates 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 取自女士开场 we need to decide by the end of the day 的「by the end of the day」，但那是「期限」而非「难以抉择的原因」；问的是 Why difficult，时间紧不是男士给出的理由，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：we need to decide by the end of the day 

 B) 张冠李戴 「很想要这份工作」对应录音后面 she is very keen about the job，那是评价 Rachel 的，且只针对一人；本题问男士为何觉得难选，他给的因是「两人都强」，不是「都很想要」，B 张冠李戴又答非所问。  借用原文：she is very keen about the job 

 C) 未提及 录音里两人对「流程」并无分歧，finalize this whole procedure 只是说要走完流程，并没有说「对 procedure 持不同看法」；C 借 procedure 一词虚构了一个原文没有的分歧。  借用原文：finalize this whole procedure

questions.prompt: What do the speakers say may be worth noting?
options: Both Rachel and Peter came across as respectful and professional.
Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school.
Both Rachel and Peter excelled in their academic pursuit.
Peter appeared slightly stronger than Rachel physically.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the speakers say may be worth noting? 

 【翻译】 说话者认为什么可能值得注意? 
 A)  Rachel和Peter都表现得既尊重他人又很专业。 
 B)  Rachel在学校的成绩略高于Peter。 
 C)  Rachel和Peter在学业追求上都很出色。 
 D)  Peter在体格上似乎略强于Rachel。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school. 
 【定位】 P4 M: The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university. But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter. 
 男：唯一也许值得一提的差别，是看起来 Rachel 在整个高中和大学的成绩略好一些。但正如我说的，只比 Peter 高出一点点。 

 【信号】 明示标记 difference worth noting 。男士直接说 The only difference worth noting，与题干 worth noting 字面对应，是教科书式的答案信号；其后 Rachel scored moderately stronger grades 加上 only a tiny bit higher than Peter 就是要抓的内容。 

 【替换】 Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university ↔ Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school stronger grades=higher grades，程度词原样保留 
 only a tiny bit higher than Peter ↔ moderately higher grades than Peter a tiny bit higher印证「略高」 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 的 respectful and professional 直接取自女士评 Peter 的 He came across as respectful and professional，是真听到的原词；但那是夸 Peter 一人的面试表现，并非两人都如此，且不是被点为「worth noting」的那点，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：He came across as respectful and professional 

 C) 与原文相反 录音强调 only a tiny bit higher，仅是「略高」；C 的 excelled（出类拔萃）且说「两人都」学业杰出，把程度从「略」拔高到「极」、把范围从「Rachel 略胜」改成「两人皆优」，与原文程度相反。  借用原文：only a tiny bit higher than Peter 

 D) 未提及 录音通篇比的是成绩、面试表现、成熟度，从未提到 physically（体格）；D 把 stronger 偷换成「身体上更强」，是录音根本没说的维度。

questions.prompt: According to the man, what might account for Peter appearing somewhat more self-assured than Rachel?
options: His use of body language.
His accumulation of experience.
His unusual state of mind.
His knowledge about the company.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to the man, what might account for Peter appearing somewhat more self-assured than Rachel? 

 【翻译】 根据男士的说法,什么可能是Peter看起来比Rachel更自信的原因? 
 A)  他对肢体语言的使用。 
 B)  他积累的经验。 
 C)  他不寻常的精神状态。 
 D)  他对公司的了解。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） His use of body language. 
 【定位】 P10 M: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow. Maybe it was something about their body language. 
 男：把他们并排比较时，是的，Peter 不知怎的显得更自信。也许跟他们的肢体语言有关。 

 【信号】 男士的归因句 Maybe it was… 。这是男士亲口给出的归因——Peter seemed more self-assured somehow 之后紧跟 Maybe it was something about their body language，用 Maybe it was… 引出原因，正是 account for 所问的答案句。 

 【替换】 Maybe it was something about their body language ↔ His use of body language body language原词同指其运用 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 的 experience 来自录音 practically no work experience，但原文说的是「两人几乎都没有工作经验」，恰恰不是经验造成差异；B 把「没有经验」偷成「经验的积累」，听到 experience 就选即落坑。  借用原文：practically no work experience 

 C) 偷换概念 录音说 Peter 显得 composed and in control of his emotions（沉着、控制情绪），是正面的镇定，并非 unusual state of mind（异常心态）；C 把镇定歪曲成「异常」，且不是男士给的归因，原文未提此因。  借用原文：composed and in control of his emotions 

 D) 张冠李戴 D 的 knowledge about the company 化用录音 asked some very good questions about the position and the company，但那是说 Rachel 问了好问题、显得很想要这份工作，针对的是 Rachel、回答的是「是否 keen」，与本题问 Peter 自信的归因无关。  借用原文：asked some very good questions about the position and the company

questions.prompt: What does the man say they will do if they can't reach an agreement?
options: Compare the candidates side by side again.
Ask the board to cast the deciding vote.
Find a way to break the tie next time.
Let John make the final decision.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say they will do if they can't reach an agreement? 

 【翻译】 男士说如果他们无法达成一致意见会怎么做? 
 A)  再次并列比较候选人。 
 B)  请董事会投决定性的一票。 
 C)  下次找个办法打破平局。 
 D)  让John做最终决定。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Let John make the final decision. 
 【定位】 P14 M: Ah, well. If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote. 
 男：啊，好吧。如果出现平局、我们没法达成一致，那我们就把它交给 John，让他来投决定票。 

 【信号】 条件句 If…then 的对策落点 。男士用 If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John 给出明确的 If…then 对策；句中专有人名 John 是强定位信号，then 后的动作即答案。 

 【替换】 take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote ↔ Let John make the final decision cast the deciding vote=make the final decision 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 的 compare side by side 取自男士早前的 When comparing them side by side，确是原词；但那是描述他们之前已做的对比，而非「谈不拢时的对策」，问的是 if can't agree 怎么办，A 时态与问点都不符。  借用原文：When comparing them side by side 

 B) 偷换概念 B 的 cast the deciding vote 正是录音原词 cast the deciding vote，极具迷惑；但录音里投决定票的是 John 一个人，B 却说交给 the board（董事会）投票，把「个人 John」偷换成「集体 board」。  借用原文：take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote 

 C) 偷换概念 C 的 break the tie 借用录音 If there's a tie 的 tie 一词，但录音对平局的对策是「这次就交给 John」，C 却说「找办法在下次打破平局」，把「当下交 John」偷改成「留待下次」，时点与做法都对不上。  借用原文：If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement

questions.prompt: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
options: The private label "L'Orange".
The woman's latest collection.
This season's new fashion.
The head designer's role.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are the speakers mainly talking about? 

 【翻译】 说话者主要在讨论什么? 
 A)  自有品牌"L'Orange" 
 B)  女士的最新系列 
 C)  本季的新时尚 
 D)  首席设计师的角色 

 【答案】 B （主旨题） The woman's latest collection. 
 【定位】 P1 We're here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L'Orange, to discuss her latest collection. 
 我们今天请到了私人时装品牌 L'Orange 的首席设计师 Clementine Ortega，来聊聊她的最新系列。 

 【信号】 开场引入语点题 。记者开场白 to discuss her latest collection 直接交代了"今天来谈什么"，访谈类对话的中心话题几乎都由开场引入句给出，这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 to discuss her latest collection ↔ The woman's latest collection. her=the woman 指代对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到品牌名 the private fashion label L'Orange，但它只是介绍设计师身份时的背景，全程没有围绕"这个品牌"展开，是听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：the private fashion label L'Orange 

 C) 偷换概念 记者后面问过 this season's look，C 借这个词把话题偷换成"本季新潮流"这种行业泛论；可对话谈的始终是"她个人的这一系列"，不是整个时尚界的趋势。  借用原文：this season's look 

 D) 未提及 录音用 head designer 介绍她的职位，D 借此说成"首席设计师的职责"；但全段没有一句在谈"这个职位要干什么"，是抓住头衔词的过度发挥。  借用原文：head designer

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she always tries to incorporate into her aesthetic?
options: Something reflecting the social norms.
Something meeting public expectations.
Something slightly absurd.
Something a bit ambiguous.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she always tries to incorporate into her aesthetic? 

 【翻译】 女士说她总是试图将什么融入她的美学风格? 
 A)  反映社会规范的东西 
 B)  符合公众期望的东西 
 C)  略微荒诞的东西 
 D)  有点模糊的东西 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Something slightly absurd. 
 【定位】 P2 Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic. 
 相反，我总是试着把一点略显荒诞的东西融入我的审美。 

 【信号】 I always try to 是直接应答 。被问者女设计师用 I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd 直接讲出她总加入的东西，主语+always 的自述句正是题干所问，是答案句。 

 【替换】 something slightly absurd ↔ Something slightly absurd. 近乎原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音里 I try not to adhere to social norms 是她要"避开"的东西，A 却说她要加入"反映社会规范"的东西，正好把否定听成了肯定。  借用原文：I try not to adhere to social norms 

 B) 与原文相反 原文 expectations 与 social norms 并列，都在 I try not to adhere to 的否定范围内；B 说她要做"符合公众期待"的东西，与她的本意相反。  借用原文：social norms and expectations 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音里 my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side 说的是她整体风格偏"含糊"，D 借 ambiguous 这个原词来答"她加入了什么"，但题问的是 incorporate 进去的具体东西（absurd），答非所问。  借用原文：my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she likes to do?
options: Merge styles often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.
Learn from the designs of the Asian rural mountain villagers.
Make velvet capes look both majestic and masculine.
Draw intricate patterns onto a traditional power suit.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she likes to do? 

 【翻译】 女士说她喜欢做什么? 
 A)  融合通常处于时尚光谱两端的风格 
 B)  向亚洲乡村山区村民的设计学习 
 C)  让天鹅绒斗篷看起来既威严又阳刚 
 D)  在传统正装西服上绘制复杂的图案 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Merge styles often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum. 
 【定位】 P6 I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum. 
 我喜欢把那些常常处于时尚光谱两端的风格融合到一起。 

 【信号】 I like to 直陈偏好 。I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum 用 I like to 直接说出她的偏好，正中题干，是答案句。 

 【替换】 merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum ↔ Merge styles often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum. 省略定语从句的同义压缩 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 录音里她去亚洲山村看了刺绣，但明说 Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile——照搬他们的设计是徒劳的，所以她没"学他们的设计"，B 把"放弃模仿"说反成"向他们学习"。  借用原文：Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile 

 C) 张冠李戴 majestic 和 masculine 是男主持人 masculine at the same time 给出的观感评价，C 盗用这两个原词，把"别人对作品的评价"伪装成"她喜欢做的事"，张冠李戴。  借用原文：masculine at the same time 

 D) 原词陷阱 I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape 是她做那件斗篷时的一次具体操作，D 把这个一次性细节冒充成她长期"喜欢做"的事，可题问的是她声明的偏好（merge styles），层级对不上。  借用原文：I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape

questions.prompt: What is the man looking forward to?
options: Obtaining the woman's signature.
Seeing the woman's new creations.
Incorporating indigenous aspects into his work.
Sharing more ideas with the woman next time.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the man looking forward to? 

 【翻译】 男士期待什么? 
 A)  获得女士的签名 
 B)  看到女士的新作品 
 C)  将本土元素融入他的作品 
 D)  下次与女士分享更多想法 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Seeing the woman's new creations. 
 【定位】 P7 we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next. 
 我们迫不及待想看看你接下来会创作出什么新作品。 

 【信号】 结尾 can't wait 表期待 。男方在结尾说 we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next，can't wait to see 就是"期待"的强信号，是答案句。 

 【替换】 to see what creations you come up with next ↔ Seeing the woman's new creations. come up with next=new creations 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 录音 your underlying signature touch 里 signature 指她"标志性"的风格印记，A 却理解成"获取她的签名"，把一词多义的 signature 偷换了义项，且男方根本没说要签名。  借用原文：your underlying signature touch 

 C) 原词陷阱 the incorporation of indigenous aspects 是男方对本季作品已完成之处的称赞，描述的是过去做成的事；C 盗用 indigenous 这个原词，把"已经做到"说成"他期待去做"，时间和主体都错位。  借用原文：the incorporation of indigenous aspects 

 D) 未提及 录音结尾的 next 是接在 what creations you come up with next（下次的作品）上的，D 借这个"下次"感造出"下次多分享想法"，可对话从没提"再聊/分享想法"，是无中生有。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about 80% of participating dogs in the new study?
options: They could readily recognize their owner simply by looking.
They could understand the implications of human commands.
They could be domesticated to act as our companions.
They could follow pointing gestures without training.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about 80% of participating dogs in the new study? 

 【翻译】 文章关于新研究中80%的参与犬只说了什么? 
 A)  它们仅通过观察就能轻易识别出自己的主人。 
 B)  它们能够理解人类指令的含义。 
 C)  它们能够被驯化成为我们的伴侣。 
 D)  它们无需训练就能跟随指向手势。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They could follow pointing gestures without training. 
 【定位】 P1 The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training. 
 研究表明，80% 参与实验的狗在从未接受过任何训练的情况下，成功跟随指点手势找到了特定地点。 

 【信号】 数字 80% 即定位锚点 。录音念到 80% of participating dogs 这个数字就是定位信号，紧跟其后的 successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training 即承载答案的那句，听到数字就该锁定后半句。 

 【替换】 followed pointing gestures ↔ follow pointing gestures 近乎原词的同动作对应 
 despite having never received prior training ↔ without training 让步从句压缩成介词短语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A readily recognize their owner simply by looking 借了录音第 1 段开头 readily understand 里的 readily 一词，但录音说的是'轻易理解命令手势'，从未说'看一眼就认出主人'，是把听到的熟词嫁接到没说过的事上。  借用原文：readily understand a wide range of their owners' commands and gestures 

 B) 偷换概念 B understand the implications of human commands 用了录音里的 commands，但 80% 那句讲的是'跟随手势找到地点'，并非'理解命令的言外之意（implications）'；implications 一词录音另有出处（讲研究意义），被挪来制造混淆。  借用原文：This could have implications in reducing conflict 

 C) 张冠李戴 C domesticated to act as our companions 的 domesticated、companions 都出自录音第 2 段讲'家养狗被驯化成伴侣'，但第 9 题问的是新研究里的 80% 流浪狗，C 把'家养狗'的事安到了'实验流浪狗'头上。  借用原文：they could function as companions and workers

questions.prompt: What may help alleviate the problem caused by stray dogs?
options: Cultivating them to be intelligent creatures.
Training them to behave like domesticated dogs.
Understanding how humans impact their behavior.
Taking measures to reduce their numbers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What may help alleviate the problem caused by stray dogs? 

 【翻译】 什么可能有助于缓解流浪犬造成的问题? 
 A)  培养它们成为聪明的生物。 
 B)  训练它们像驯化犬一样行事。 
 C)  理解人类如何影响它们的行为。 
 D)  采取措施减少它们的数量。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Understanding how humans impact their behavior. 
 【定位】 P3 Understanding how humans shape stray dogs' behavior may help alleviate this problem. 
 理解人类如何塑造流浪狗的行为，可能有助于缓解这一问题。 

 【信号】 help alleviate 即办法落点 。录音第 3 段 may help alleviate this problem 与题干 alleviate the problem 完全呼应，这句的主语 Understanding how humans shape stray dogs' behavior 就是'有助于缓解'的那件事，help 一出现即落点。 

 【替换】 Understanding how humans shape stray dogs' behavior ↔ Understanding how humans impact their behavior 同义动词替换 shape=impact 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A Cultivating them to be intelligent creatures 借了录音 stray dogs are intelligent creatures 里的 intelligent creatures，但原文是'流浪狗本就是聪明的生物'，并没说'培养它们变聪明'能缓解问题，盗原词却扭了意思。  借用原文：stray dogs are intelligent creatures 

 B) 与原文相反 B Training them to behave like domesticated dogs 拼了录音的 training、domesticated，但全文恰恰强调流浪狗'未经训练'也能懂人、应'给空间善待'，'训练成家养狗'与文章主张方向相反。  借用原文：dogs that are highly responsive to human commands and gestures 

 D) 未提及 D Taking measures to reduce their numbers（采取措施减少其数量）录音全篇未提'减少流浪狗数量'，是凭'流浪狗是问题'想当然推出的极端办法，原文谈的是'理解与善待'而非清除。

questions.prompt: What do the researchers suggest we do to reduce conflicts between stray dogs and humans?
options: Tame them through repeated training.
Treat them with sensitivity and respect.
Make them responsive to our commands.
Watch their behavior and try to improve it.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the researchers suggest we do to reduce conflicts between stray dogs and humans? 

 【翻译】 研究人员建议我们做什么来减少流浪犬与人类之间的冲突? 
 A)  通过反复训练驯服它们。 
 B)  以敏感和尊重的态度对待它们。 
 C)  使它们对我们的指令做出反应。 
 D)  观察它们的行为并尝试改善。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Treat them with sensitivity and respect. 
 【定位】 P3 Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect, and giving them space, the researchers assert, can reduce much conflict. 
 研究者断言，以体贴和尊重对待流浪狗、给它们空间，可以大大减少冲突。 

 【信号】 researchers assert 即建议落点 。录音末句 the researchers assert, can reduce much conflict 里 the researchers assert（研究者断言）正是建议信号，与题干 suggest 对应；其前的 Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect 就是被建议的做法。 

 【替换】 Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect ↔ Treat them with sensitivity and respect 动名词转祈使、近乎原词 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A Tame them through repeated training 借了全文反复出现的 training，但研究者主张'善待、给空间'，且全文强调流浪狗'未经训练也能懂人'，'反复训练驯服'与建议方向相反。  借用原文：such dogs have never been trained 

 C) 张冠李戴 C Make them responsive to our commands 用了录音第 2 段 highly responsive to human commands，但那是描述'家养狗被驯化后的结果'，并非研究者对'如何减少流浪狗冲突'的建议，对象与语境都错位。  借用原文：highly responsive to human commands and gestures 

 D) 偷换概念 D Watch their behavior and try to improve it 蹭了录音 They closely observe humans 的 observe/behavior，但原文是说'狗观察人'，且研究者建议是'善待给空间'，并非'人观察狗的行为并改进它'，主客颠倒且非建议内容。  借用原文：They closely observe humans and use their understanding of us

questions.prompt: Why is food product placement within the fridge very important?
options: The temperature inside it varies from place to place.
Proper placement facilitates access to food products.
Its different shelves are designed for different purposes.
The space in an average fridge changes from top to bottom.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why is food product placement within the fridge very important? 

 【翻译】 为什么冰箱内食品摆放位置非常重要? 
 A)  冰箱内部各处温度不同。 
 B)  恰当的摆放便于取用食品。 
 C)  冰箱不同的搁板是为不同目的设计的。 
 D)  普通冰箱从上到下的空间各不相同。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The temperature inside it varies from place to place. 
 【定位】 P1 The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between. Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize. 
 普通冰箱内部的温度实际上从前到后、从下到上以及中间各处都不一样。正因如此，食物在冰箱内的摆放位置远比你以为的重要得多。 

 【信号】 Because of this 因果回指 。Because of this 是答案信号：this 回指前一句讲的温度处处不同，紧接着说正因如此摆放才重要，所以前一句 The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies 就是位置重要的原因。 

 【替换】 The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between ↔ The temperature inside it varies from place to place. 处处不同概括为因地而异 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Proper placement facilitates access to food products. 说摆放是为了方便取放，但录音解释的原因只有温度因位置而异，全程没提取放是否方便，属于录音未提及的角度。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Its different shelves are designed for different purposes. 听起来很对，但它说的是层架被设计成不同用途，而录音第一段给的原因是温度因位置而异；它借后文反复出现的 shelf 字眼制造听到就想选的诱惑，却答非所问。  借用原文：The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge 

 D) 偷换概念 The space in an average fridge changes from top to bottom. 几乎照搬录音句式，却把变化的主语从温度换成了空间 space；录音说的是 The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies，变的是温度不是空间，属偷换核心概念。  借用原文：The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between

questions.prompt: What does the passage say is the whole purpose of the modern refrigerator?
options: To slow the rising of temperature in it.
To provide a big box of evenly cold air.
To prevent germs from growing quickly.
To keep the food cold as long as possible.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say is the whole purpose of the modern refrigerator? 

 【翻译】 文章认为现代冰箱的全部目的是什么? 
 A)  减缓冰箱内温度上升。 
 B)  提供一个温度均匀的低温大空间。 
 C)  防止细菌快速生长。 
 D)  尽可能长时间地保持食物低温。 

 【答案】 C （目的题） To prevent germs from growing quickly. 
 【定位】 P2 The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria, which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 degrees Celsius. 
 现代冰箱的根本目的是减缓细菌的生长，这些细菌在 4.4 到 60 摄氏度之间会大量繁殖。 

 【信号】 purpose is to 直接点明 。The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria 用 purpose is to 把目的直接说出，是最强的答案信号，听到 purpose 就该锁定其后的 to do 内容。 

 【替换】 to slow the growth of bacteria ↔ To prevent germs from growing quickly. bacteria=germs，slow growth=prevent growing quickly 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 To slow the rising of temperature in it. 借用了录音里反复出现的 temperature 字眼，把目的说成减缓升温；但录音明说目的是 to slow the growth of bacteria，减缓的是细菌生长不是温度上升，盗词却答错对象。  借用原文：to slow the growth of bacteria 

 B) 与原文相反 To provide a big box of evenly cold air. 几乎照搬录音开头 one big box of evenly cold air，但那是录音先抛出又立刻否定（Not so）的错误印象，并非冰箱目的，盗用否定前的说法。  借用原文：Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air? Not so! 

 D) 未提及 To keep the food cold as long as possible. 是凭常识容易选的诱饵，听起来冰箱不就是保冷吗；但录音点明的目的是抑制细菌生长，没说根本目的是尽量久保冷，属未提及的常识陷阱。

questions.prompt: Where in the fridge should we store foods already cooked?
options: On the top shelf.
In the middle section.
On the inside of its doors.
At the back of its bottom shelf.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Where in the fridge should we store foods already cooked? 

 【翻译】 已经烹饪好的食物应该存放在冰箱的什么位置? 
 A)  最上层搁板。 
 B)  中间部分。 
 C)  冰箱门内侧。 
 D)  冰箱底层搁板后部。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） On the top shelf. 
 【定位】 P3 Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf. 
 把即食或已经煮熟的食物放在顶层。 

 【信号】 对象+位置直接配对 。Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf 把对象 already cooked 与位置 the top shelf 直接配在一句里，信号就是题干所问食物原词出现处，紧跟其后的就是位置。 

 【替换】 on the top shelf ↔ On the top shelf. 位置词原样对应 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 In the middle section. 盗用录音里真实出现的 middle shelf，但录音说中层最恒温、用来放 eggs，不是放熟食；听到 middle 就选会答非所问。  借用原文：The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here. 

 C) 原词陷阱 On the inside of its doors. 盗用录音的 inside of refrigerator doors，但录音说门内温度不稳、要避免放易腐食物，并未指派熟食，张冠李戴。  借用原文：Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors...refrain from putting perishable foods in there. 

 D) 原词陷阱 At the back of its bottom shelf. 盗用录音真实位置 back of the bottom shelf，但录音说那里最冷、用来放 perishable dairy products，不是熟食，盗位置却对错食物。  借用原文：The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here

questions.prompt: Why should we never store foods with high water content at the back of the bottom shelf?
options: They will be extra-chilly.
They will be hard to defrost.
They will be contaminated.
They will be ruined.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why should we never store foods with high water content at the back of the bottom shelf? 

 【翻译】 为什么我们绝不应该把含水量高的食物存放在底层搁板后部? 
 A)  它们会变得格外冰冷。 
 B)  它们会难以解冻。 
 C)  它们会被污染。 
 D)  它们会被毁坏。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They will be ruined. 
 【定位】 P3 Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them. 
 绝不要把含水量高的食物放在这里，因为它们里面的水会结冰，等于把它们毁了。 

 【信号】 because 引出后果 。because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them 由 because 引出禁止的原因，effectively ruining them 是落点后果，because 后到句末就是答案句。 

 【替换】 effectively ruining them ↔ They will be ruined. ruining 主动转被动 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They will be extra-chilly. 借用录音前文出现的 extra-chilly 字眼，但那词是讲顶层不必放需要极冷的食物，与底层含水食物被毁无关；底层后果是结冰损坏不是单纯变冷。  借用原文：save it for the foods that don't need extra-chilly temperatures 

 B) 过度推断 They will be hard to defrost. 顺着结冰往下想出难以解冻，但录音只说结冰把食物毁了，没提解冻难易，属在结冰基础上多推一步。 
 C) 未提及 They will be contaminated. 说会被污染，但录音讲的后果是结冰损坏，全程没提污染，属录音未涉及的角度。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is quite common among older people?
options: Chronic depression.
Growing feebleness.
Hip fracture.
Fatal infections.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say is quite common among older people? 

 【翻译】 说话者说在老年人中什么是相当常见的? 
 A)  慢性抑郁症。 
 B)  日益虚弱。 
 C)  髋部骨折。 
 D)  致命性感染。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Hip fracture. 
 【定位】 P2 In one project we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event and we're trying to understand the impact of depression. 
 在一个项目里，我们研究老年人的髋部骨折，这是一种常见的情况，我们想弄清抑郁对它的影响。 

 【信号】 which is a common event 直接点"常见" 。答案句里 which is a common event（这是一种常见的情况）紧跟在 hip fracture in older people 之后，which 指代的正是 hip fracture，这个"常见"信号词把答案锁死在髋部骨折上。 

 【替换】 hip fracture in older people, which is a common event ↔ Hip fracture. 原词直接对应＋common 坐实 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到 depression，A 的 Chronic depression. 借此勾人，但原文说的是"骨折后常发展出抑郁"，抑郁是骨折带来的结果，且并未被 common 修饰，也没说是"chronic（慢性）"，答非所问。  借用原文：these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音说 become feeble a lot more quickly，B 的 Growing feebleness. 取了这个 feeble，但原文讲的是骨折＋抑郁导致"更快变虚弱"这一恶化进程，并非在说"老年人中常见的是虚弱"，对不上题干的"常见"。  借用原文：become feeble a lot more quickly than others 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音说 They get infections. Often these infections lead to death.，D 的 Fatal infections. 拼合了 infections 和"致命"，但原文 often 修饰的是"感染导致死亡"这一后续后果，处于"骨折→抑郁→虚弱→感染→死亡"链条末端，不是题干问的"常见之事"本身。  借用原文：Often these infections lead to death.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think excites her most about her research?
options: It feels real and relevant.
It contributes to psychology.
It outcompetes lots of academics' research.
It wins recognition outside of Birmingham.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker think excites her most about her research? 

 【翻译】 说话者认为她的研究最令她兴奋的是什么? 
 A)  它让人感觉真实且切题。 
 B)  它对心理学有贡献。 
 C)  它胜过许多学者的研究。 
 D)  它在Birmingham之外赢得认可。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） It feels real and relevant. 
 【定位】 P4 I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant. 
 我认为我的研究最让我兴奋的地方，在于它让人感到真实而切身相关。 

 【信号】 excites me most 直接领出答案 。答案句 the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant 里 excites me most 与题干 excites her most 是同一表态信号，is that 后面那句就是她给出的理由，定位精准。 

 【替换】 it feels real and relevant ↔ It feels real and relevant. 几乎原句搬入选项 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音确有 from the perspective of the psychologist，B 的 It contributes to psychology. 借 psychology 勾人，但原文是说"不再只从心理学家的单一视角看"，恰恰在强调超越心理学，而非"为心理学做贡献"，意思反向。  借用原文：rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist 

 C) 过度推断 录音说 Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant，C 的 It outcompetes lots of academics' research. 借 academics 勾人，但原文只是用别的学者作对比来突出"自己的研究更切身相关"，从未说"胜过／outcompete"别人，属过度拔高。  借用原文：Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them 

 D) 原词陷阱 Birmingham 是录音里反复出现的地名（见 The impact that my research will have in Birmingham），D 的 It wins recognition outside of Birmingham. 借它勾人，但录音从没说研究"在伯明翰之外赢得认可"，只说这是"全球性问题"，把"问题是全球的"偷换成"研究在外地获认可"。  借用原文：But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK. This is a problem globally.

questions.prompt: How does the speaker approach her research project?
options: By bringing together experts old and young.
By counting on advanced modern technology.
By making full use of her expertise.
By combining multiple perspectives.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does the speaker approach her research project? 

 【翻译】 说话者如何开展她的研究项目? 
 A)  通过把年长和年轻的专家聚集在一起。 
 B)  通过依靠先进的现代技术。 
 C)  通过充分利用她的专业知识。 
 D)  通过结合多种视角。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） By combining multiple perspectives. 
 【定位】 P4 rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health. 
 与其只采取单一视角，与其只从心理学家的角度看待衰老与健康，我们现在汇集了许多不同的技术和许多不同的观点，来真正审视影响健康的各种因素。 

 【信号】 rather than… we are now bringing together 对比转折 。答案句用 rather than just taking one perspective 先否定"单一视角"，再以 we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints 给出真正做法，"不是A而是B"的对比让 B 半句成为答案落点。 

 【替换】 a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints ↔ By combining multiple perspectives. different viewpoints＝multiple perspectives 同义改写 
 bringing together ↔ combining bring together＝combine 同义动词 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确有 bringing together，A 的 By bringing together experts old and young. 借此勾人，但原文汇集的是 different techniques and viewpoints（技术与观点），不是"老少专家"，old and young 是套用别处的 older／young 之类印象，张冠李戴。  借用原文：we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints 

 B) 过度推断 录音说 a lot of different techniques（多种不同的技术手段），B 的 By counting on advanced modern technology. 借 techniques 勾人，但原文只说"多种技术手段"，从没说"依赖先进的现代科技"，advanced modern 是凭空添加的拔高。  借用原文：bringing together a lot of different techniques 

 C) 与原文相反 By making full use of her expertise. 即"充分用她自己（心理学家）的专长"，这正是录音用 rather than… just from the perspective of the psychologist 明确否定的单一视角做法，选项取了被否定的那一半，与原文意思相反。  借用原文：rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about most colleges and graduate schools in America?
options: They don't teach basic organization.
They don't focus on teaching techniques.
They attach little importance to recipes.
They hire very few distinguished chefs.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about most colleges and graduate schools in America? 

 【翻译】 说话者对美国大多数学院和研究生院有何看法? 
 A)  它们不教授基本的组织方法。 
 B)  它们不注重教学技巧。 
 C)  它们不重视配方。 
 D)  它们雇用的杰出厨师很少。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They don't teach basic organization. 
 【定位】 P2 The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do. 
 这个市场之所以巨大，部分原因在于大多数大学和研究生院并不教授基本的组织方法，而烹饪学校和专业厨房却教。 

 【信号】 原因状语 because 引出的因果句 。答案句由 partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization 这个 because 因果结构托出，讲者在解释“市场为何巨大”时正面说出了学校“不教什么”，这种交代原因的从句往往就是细节答案所在。 

 【替换】 most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization ↔ They don't teach basic organization. 把主语换成代词，其余几乎照搬 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 选项 They don't focus on teaching techniques. 借了录音开头 recipes and techniques 里的 techniques 制造熟耳感，但讲者从没说学校“不重视教技巧”，学校被说成不教的是 organization，不是 techniques，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：recipes and techniques 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 They attach little importance to recipes. 取了开头 recipes and techniques 的 recipes，但录音并未说学校“不重视食谱”，更没把 recipes 和大学挂钩，是借原词编出的无中生有。  借用原文：recipes and techniques 

 D) 未提及 选项 They hire very few distinguished chefs. 用了贯穿全篇的 chefs 蹭话题，但录音通篇没提“学校聘用名厨多少”，hire very few distinguished chefs 完全是没听到的内容。  借用原文：celebrity chefs

questions.prompt: How do students of the culinary institute of America view "mise-en-place" or "put in place"?
options: It's unique to celebrity chefs.
It's a way of transformation.
It's too demanding for them.
It's a way of life to them.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How do students of the culinary institute of America view "mise-en-place" or "put in place"? 

 【翻译】 美国烹饪学院的学生如何看待"mise-en-place"或"就位"? 
 A)  这是名厨独有的。 
 B)  这是一种转变方式。 
 C)  这对他们要求过高。 
 D)  对他们来说这是一种生活方式。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） It's a way of life to them. 
 【定位】 P4 Students at the culinary institute of America view it as a way of life. 
 美国烹饪学院的学生把它视为一种生活方式。 

 【信号】 被点名群体后紧跟的“view it as…”态度句 。讲者点出 Students at the culinary institute of America 这一群体后，紧接 view it as a way of life 直接给出他们的看法，这种“某群人 + view/see it as……”的句子就是态度题的标准答案落点。 

 【替换】 view it as a way of life ↔ It's a way of life to them. view it as A 改写成 It's A to them 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 选项 It's unique to celebrity chefs. 借了开头 celebrity chefs 的熟词，但录音说把它当生活方式的是学生，不是名厨独有；unique（独有）这个范围限定录音根本没说，属偷换概念加原词诱选。  借用原文：celebrity chefs 

 B) 答非所问 选项 It's a way of transformation. 取自录音 transforms the lives of its practitioners 的 transform，听起来很耳熟，但那句是讲者总述 mise-en-place 的功效，不是“学生怎么看它”的答案；题问的是学生的 view，答案句明确是 a way of life。  借用原文：transforms the lives of its practitioners 

 C) 过度推断 选项 It's too demanding for them. 利用 focus and self-discipline 让人联想“很苛刻”，但录音从未说学生觉得它“太苛刻”，反而把它当生活方式正面接纳，too demanding 是凭印象的过度推断。  借用原文：focus and self-discipline

questions.prompt: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?
options: Respect others so as to be respected.
Use time and resources in a wise way.
Cultivate a habit of self-discipline.
Learn from philosophers earnestly.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk? 

 【翻译】 说话者在讲话结尾建议我们做什么? 
 A)  尊重他人以获得尊重。 
 B)  明智地使用时间和资源。 
 C)  培养自律的习惯。 
 D)  认真向哲学家学习。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Use time and resources in a wise way. 
 【定位】 P6 But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious, your self-respect and the respect of others are precious. Use them wisely. 
 但在最高层次上去实践，mise-en-place 告诉我们：时间是宝贵的，资源是宝贵的，空间是宝贵的，你的自尊和对他人的尊重都是宝贵的。要明智地使用它们。 

 【信号】 结尾的祈使劝告句“Use them wisely” 。整段在罗列 time is precious, resources are precious 之后，以祈使句 Use them wisely. 收束，这句独立成句的劝告正是讲者在结尾给出的建议，是答案的落点。 

 【替换】 time is precious, resources are precious ↔ Use time and resources in a wise way. 把要珍惜的对象同义搬进祈使句 
 Use them wisely. ↔ in a wise way wisely 改写成 in a wise way 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Respect others so as to be respected. 借了 your self-respect and the respect of others are precious 里的 respect，但录音只把“尊重”列为“宝贵之物”之一，最后的劝告是 Use them wisely（明智使用），并非“尊重别人以换取被尊重”，且 so as to be respected 是录音没有的因果，属原词陷阱加过度推断。  借用原文：your self-respect and the respect of others are precious 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 Cultivate a habit of self-discipline. 取自第四段 focus and self-discipline 的 self-discipline，这是前文描述 mise-en-place 作用时的词，不是结尾劝告；题问 at the end，结尾讲者劝的是明智使用时间资源，不是培养自律。  借用原文：focus and self-discipline 

 D) 偷换概念 选项 Learn from philosophers earnestly. 利用结尾 Isn't that a philosophy for our time? 的 philosophy 设套，但那只是反问“这难道不是我们时代的一种哲理吗”，并非叫人“认真向哲学家学习”，philosophers 与 learn from 都是录音没有的捏造。  借用原文：Isn't that a philosophy for our time?

questions.prompt: What should self-acceptance be used as according to the speaker?
options: The motive for hard work.
The reason for stagnation.
The basis for self-improvement.
The justification for self-confidence.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should self-acceptance be used as according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 根据讲话者的观点,自我接纳应该被用作什么? 
 A)  努力工作的动机。 
 B)  停滞不前的理由。 
 C)  自我提升的基础。 
 D)  自信的正当理由。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The basis for self-improvement. 
 【定位】 P1 The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth. 
 我们在这件事上犯的错误是：尽管自我接纳至关重要，但它其实应当被用作成长的基础。 

 【信号】 转折 whilst + 定性结构 used as 。答案句先用让步 whilst self-acceptance is imperative（尽管自我接纳重要）退一步，再用 it should actually be used as the basis for growth 给出真正主张，actually 加重了转折后的落点，正是这句对 self-acceptance 做了定性。 

 【替换】 used as the basis for growth ↔ The basis for self-improvement. growth = self-improvement 同义替换 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 The motive for hard work. 把 self-acceptance 说成『努力工作的动机』，原文只讲它是成长的基础，从未提 hard work，也未提 motive，属无中生有。 
 B) 原词陷阱 The reason for stagnation. 借用了原文 we tend to stagnate 的同根词 stagnation 制造耳熟，但原文说『不成长才会停滞』，stagnation 是不接纳成长的后果，绝非 self-acceptance 被用作的角色，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：we tend to stagnate 

 D) 偷换概念 The justification for self-confidence. 利用 self- 前缀与 C 的 self-improvement 混淆，但原文落点是 growth/improvement，不是 self-confidence，且 justification（理由）也非原文的 basis，属偷换概念。  借用原文：the basis for growth

questions.prompt: What do people tend to do when they have reached midlife?
options: Feel confidence, happiness and satisfaction.
Believe they have achieved their life goals.
Use a key tool for setting ambitious goals.
Stop imagining further progress in life.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do people tend to do when they have reached midlife? 

 【翻译】 当人们步入中年时,他们往往会做什么? 
 A)  感到自信、幸福和满足。 
 B)  相信他们已经实现了人生目标。 
 C)  使用一个关键工具来设定雄心勃勃的目标。 
 D)  停止想象人生中的进一步进步。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Stop imagining further progress in life. 
 【定位】 P2 Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting. ... We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be. 
 然而正如常见的那样，到我们步入中年时，我们已经不再梦想自己想要实现什么，并对设定目标抱有相当负面的感受。……我们不再去想象自己想过的生活或想成为的人。 

 【信号】 转折 Yet + midlife 时间锚 + 重复 stop 。Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife 用 Yet 转折并点出时间锚 midlife，随后 we've stopped dreaming 与 We stop imagining the life we'd like to have 两次出现 stop，反复强调的负向行为正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be ↔ Stop imagining further progress in life. stop imagining 原词 + 概括化 
 we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve ↔ Stop imagining further progress in life. stop dreaming = stop imagining progress 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 Feel confidence, happiness and satisfaction. 三个词全部来自原文 Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals，但原文前面是 Instead of（而不是），意思恰恰是人们没有这些感受，选项却取了被否定的内容，是典型听到原词就选的陷阱。  借用原文：Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals 

 B) 与原文相反 Believe they have achieved their life goals. 说人们相信已达成人生目标，而原文说中年时人们 feel we are always falling short（总觉得没达到），方向完全相反，属无中生有又反向。  借用原文：we feel we are always falling short 

 C) 张冠李戴 Use a key tool for setting ambitious goals. 里 a key tool 来自第 2 段开头 A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination，但那是作者讲『工具是什么』，并非说中年人会去用它；原文恰恰说中年时人们停止了想象，选项张冠李戴。  借用原文：A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination

questions.prompt: Why do we find ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal?
options: We feel we are always falling behind others.
We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal.
There are various misconceptions about goal setting.
There are always problems with the goal originally set.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do we find ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal? 

 【翻译】 为什么我们会因未能达成目标而感到恼怒? 
 A)  我们觉得自己总是落后于他人。 
 B)  我们必须适应不断变化的目标。 
 C)  关于目标设定存在各种误解。 
 D)  最初设定的目标总是存在问题。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal. 
 【定位】 P4 The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not. 
 我们因没达成目标而恼火，问题在于：目标总在变化，而无论我们是否意识到，我们也总在不断适应。 

 【信号】 因果结构 The problem with … is because 。The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes 用 The problem … is because 直接给出原因，because 后的 the goal always changes and we're always adapting 就是答案句核心。 

 【替换】 the goal always changes and we're always adapting ↔ We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal. always changes + always adapting → ever-changing + adapt 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 We feel we are always falling behind others. 借了原文反复出现的 always 与 falling 的语感（如 we feel we are always falling short），但加了 others（落后于他人）。原文讲的是和自己的目标比、和来路比，从未说和别人比，others 是凭空添加。  借用原文：we feel we are always falling short 

 C) 原词陷阱 There are various misconceptions about goal setting. 搬用了原文 herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions 的 misconceptions，听着耳熟，但题目问的是『恼火的原因』，原因是 the goal always changes，而非泛泛地说『存在各种误解』，属听到原词就选的陷阱。  借用原文：herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions 

 D) 偷换概念 There are always problems with the goal originally set. 借了原文 The problem with… 的 problem 一词，但原文说的是『恼火这件事的问题在于目标在变』，不是说『当初设的目标本身有毛病』，把问题归错了对象。  借用原文：The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say has an immediate positive impact on our thinking?
options: A noticeable change in the number of goals to achieve.
Measuring always against the gap rather than the gain.
Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal.
A proper conception of what we fail to notice in trying to achieve our goals.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say has an immediate positive impact on our thinking? 

 【翻译】 讲话者说什么对我们的思维有立即的积极影响? 
 A)  要实现的目标数量发生明显变化。 
 B)  总是根据差距而非收获来衡量。 
 C)  衡量我们从哪里来而不是根据目标来衡量。 
 D)  对我们在努力实现目标时未能注意到的事物有恰当的理解。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal. 
 【定位】 P4 We measure against the goal, rather than where we've come from. ... In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results. ... It's a simple, yet profound change in perception ... yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking. 
 我们对着目标来衡量，而不是衡量自己走过了多远。……当我们衡量自己走过了多远、而非衡量离要去的地方还差多少时，我们就看到了成果。……这是一种简单却深刻的认知转变……却对我们的思维有着即时而正面的影响。 

 【信号】 正面评价 profound/positive impact 指向 measuring where we've come from 。has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking 这句的『它』回指前文反复强调的 In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to，作者用 profound、positive impact 正面定性的正是这种衡量来路的做法。 

 【替换】 measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to ↔ Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal. rather than = instead of，goal = where we're trying to get to 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A noticeable change in the number of goals to achieve. 说『要达成的目标数量发生明显变化』，原文谈的是衡量基准的转变（量来路 vs 量目标），从未提目标的数量变化，属未提及。 
 B) 与原文相反 Measuring always against the gap rather than the gain. 搬用了原文术语 We measure always against the goal 与 gap/gain，但作者批评的恰恰是『总对着 gap/goal 量』、推崇的是量 gain（来路）。选项说『量 gap 而非 gain』正好取了被否定的一面，与原文相反。  借用原文：We measure always against the goal 

 D) 偷换概念 A proper conception of what we fail to notice in trying to achieve our goals. 借了原文 things we've taken for granted, or not noticed 的 not noticed，拼成『对我们没注意到之物的正确认知』，但原文说有即时正面影响的是『衡量来路这一做法』本身，不是某种 conception，属偷换概念/过度拼凑。  借用原文：things we've taken for granted, or not noticed
